newsitem.title: USA: DLJ cuts online stock trade commissions to $20.
newsitem.headline: DLJ cuts online stock trade commissions to $20.

text.p: Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Inc. said Tuesday it has significantly expanded its online brokerage service and will reduce commissions for online stock transactions to a flat fee of $20 as of June 20.
The firm also said the nine-year-old service, PC Financial Network -- http://www.pcfn.com, has been renamed DLJ Direct.
DLJ Direct will allow qualified online investors to invest in DLJ lead-managed initial public offerings beginning this summer.
Starting in September, online investors will also be able to gain time-delayed access to earnings estimates, research summaries and economic analysis prepared by DLJ's equity analysts, the firm said.

"These changes make DLJ the first major investment bank to offer online investors access to a comprehensive range of its own trading services, investment research and financial products," the firm said in a statement.
DLJ said the no-frills online discount brokerage service launched in 1988 now has more than 320,000 accounts with assets of more than $3.2 billion.

The firm said DLJ Direct is geared for the sophisticated and active, but self-directed investor. It is available to users of the Internet, members of America Online, Prodigy, CompuServe, Microsoft Investor and Reuters Money Network.
DLJ's stock fell 25 cents to $48 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
